---
title: "Second reader expectations"
subtitle: "Read this if you would like me to serve as a thesis second reader"
---

These notes are intended to manage bilateral expectations. In my experience,
explicit expectations on both sides make things more efficient and more
productive. Timing can be tight at the end of a student's time at NPS, so part of
the purpose here is to help you plan your thesis workflow schedule.

My approach as second reader is to support you in preparing a written thesis
consistent with the expectations of the MAE Department, NPS, and the general
engineering science academic community. Normally the second reader is not involved
regularly with the research, though all NPS faculty are ready to help any student
with domain-specific questions. If the second reader is expected to be a regular
contributor to the research effort, it is probably more appropriate to modify the
role to that of co-advisor.

## What I expect

- You will review my [technical writing
  notes](../thesis-prep/technical-writing.qmd) before developing your final draft,
  and your draft will be free of the common mistakes addressed there.
- I will be asked to review a final draft of your complete thesis document only
  **after your advisor has reviewed and signed off on the document**.
- You will give me a minimum of one week's notice of when to expect your completed
  draft.
- You will send me the draft electronically as a PDF. Box or OneDrive is best for
  large files.
- I will have at least one week to review the document and get it back to you. I
  will return it electronically with comments and edits.
- Addressing the comments and edits can typically happen quickly, but you should
  plan time to make corrections.
- I do not need to re-review the draft. I expect you will address all the comments,
  edits, and questions provided, and will ask for clarification if you need more
  detail on a specific issue.

## What you can expect

- I will be available for specific questions while you work on your research and
  your thesis.
- Once I have advance notice of when to expect your draft, I will block out a few
  hours to review it within one week — hopefully sooner.
- I will return your draft with electronic notes. My opinions as second reader are
  secondary to your primary advisor's guidance; if our recommendations conflict,
  follow your advisor.
- Unless I say otherwise on the returned draft, we do not need to meet to go over
  the comments. They are intended to stand alone, and I assume you will address
  them all before submitting the final document.
- If you have questions about the comments, or other follow-up questions, you can
  schedule time to work together to finalize the draft.
